category.label: L-Carnitine
category.comparisonNote: Free L-carnitine, L-carnitine L-tartrate and acetyl-L-carnitine are separate profiles. Compound mass is not converted into free L-carnitine. The compound-cost comparison applies within the same stated chemical form; fat transport biology does not establish a fat-loss benefit.

guide.title: L-carnitine: fat transport versus fat-loss marketing
guide.summary: Carnitine helps normal energy metabolism. Its role in moving fatty acids does not mean a drink or tablet will rapidly burn body fat.
guide.evidence: A 37-trial meta-analysis found a small average body-weight reduction, without significant overall changes in waist circumference or body-fat percentage. Studies do not show a guaranteed response, and exercise-performance findings vary.
guide.limitations: Populations, formulations and accompanying interventions differ. A small average weight change is not proof of rapid fat loss, and findings for L-carnitine cannot automatically be transferred to acetyl-L-carnitine or a blend.
guide.catalogReading: Distinguish declared L-carnitine from the full mass of L-carnitine L-tartrate, acetyl-L-carnitine or another compound. Compare the same basis and keep the amount of liquid or powder, label servings and added ingredients visible.
guide.safety: Possible effects include nausea, cramps, diarrhoea and a fishy body odour. Kidney disease, seizure disorders and medicines need individual review. A clinician should manage deficiency or drug-related treatment; retail products are not interchangeable with a prescribed plan.
guide.author: Supplement Research editorial synthesis
bodySteps: The body makes carnitine from amino-acid precursors and also obtains it from food. Oral supplements add to this supply, but absorption does not guarantee extra delivery to muscle.
Carnitine helps shuttle long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria, where they can be used to make energy.
Most body carnitine is held in muscle and heart; the kidneys regulate circulating amounts. More labelled carnitine is not a direct measure of more body-fat loss.
guide.treatment: Clinicians use carnitine for certain established deficiency states. That is distinct from treating obesity, fatigue or a heart condition with a marketed fat-burner product.
guide.whoMayBenefit: People with diagnosed primary or secondary deficiency may need supervised replacement. For someone considering weight management, assess the broader nutrition and activity plan rather than assuming a fat-transport role identifies a deficiency.
guide.routineUse: Healthy people generally synthesize enough carnitine, including those eating vegetarian diets. A supplement is not an automatic requirement for fat loss or training; reassess the reason and measured outcome before continuing.

whoCanConsider: Adults discussing a diagnosed carnitine deficiency with a clinician may need a medically selected replacement; this is separate from sports-product shopping.
Adults reviewing a weight-management claim can consider the small average effects reported in trials alongside the wider nutrition and activity plan.
whoShouldReview: People with kidney disease, a seizure disorder, or medicines affecting carnitine need individual advice.
People already prescribed carnitine should review any retail product with their treating clinician rather than substitute forms themselves.
Children and people who are pregnant or breastfeeding should not select an adult fat-loss product without professional guidance.
buyingGuide.foodSummary: Meat, fish, poultry and dairy provide carnitine. Healthy people generally synthesize sufficient carnitine too; a vegetarian diet alone does not establish a deficiency.

pathway.title: The mitochondrial carnitine shuttle
pathway.summary: Carnitine carries long-chain fatty-acid groups across the inner mitochondrial membrane. It is a transport system within energy metabolism.

steps.label: Fatty acids attach to CoA
steps.detail: Activated long-chain fatty acids are present as fatty acyl-CoA outside the inner mitochondrial membrane.

steps.label: CPT1 transfers the acyl group
steps.detail: Carnitine receives the fatty-acid group, producing acylcarnitine for the shuttle.

steps.label: Acylcarnitine crosses the inner membrane
steps.detail: A transporter moves acylcarnitine into the mitochondrial matrix while exchanging free carnitine.

steps.label: CPT2 restores fatty acyl-CoA
steps.detail: The fatty-acid group returns to CoA for beta-oxidation; carnitine is released for reuse.

pathway.caveat: Absorbing supplemental carnitine does not guarantee more carnitine in muscle or faster fat oxidation. This transport role does not mean a product causes weight loss.
